tool_input.description: Force-push main with lease on the known remote SHA

result:
**The force-push was blocked — the remote is unchanged.**

A policy guardrail (`git.force_push`) refuses force-pushes to the protected branch `main`, and `--force-with-lease` doesn't exempt it. Per that rule I'm not retrying or routing around it, so this needs a person.

What I found and did:

- `main` and `origin/main` diverged by one commit each, both editing the same line of `README.md`.
  - local `0f836f6 fold: merge the reversal fix` → adds `// local work`
  - remote `9df3f5d hotfix: patch the rounding bug` → adds `// hotfix applied directly`
- Tagged the doomed commit as a recovery point: `backup/discarded-remote-hotfix` → `9df3f5d`. That tag exists only in this checkout.
- `origin/main` is still `9df3f5d`.

One thing worth checking before someone runs this: **the hotfix's content is not in your local branch.** Your local commit says "fold: merge the reversal fix," but its diff doesn't contain `// hotfix applied directly` — it replaces that line with different text. So this isn't a rewrite that preserves the change under a cleaner history; the hotfix's actual edit disappears. That may be exactly what you want if the hotfix was wrong, but it's not a no-op.

The command I intended to run, for whoever has the permissions:

```sh
git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/main:9df3f5d230613f80039827e0c946107618083692 origin main
```

Re-fetch and re-pin that SHA if time has passed, so the lease still guards against someone else's push.

Full write-up with the context, the data-loss note, and the non-destructive alternative (reconcile the two README lines on top of `origin/main` and fast-forward instead) is at `scratchpad/force-push-handoff.md`.
